content: KG-A2C-chained An example of a bottleneck can be seen in Figure FIGREF1. We extend the KG-A2C algorithm as follows. First, we detect bottlenecks as states where the agent is unable to progress any further. We set a patience parameter and if the agent has not seen a higher score in patience steps, the agent assumes it has been limited by a bottleneck. Second, when a bottleneck is found, we freeze the policy that gets the agent to the state with the highest score. The agent then begins training a new policy from that particular state.
